title: And Is the Gospel Peace and Love
description: And Is the Gospel Peace and Love in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 357 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Example of the Saviour”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: And is the gos-pel peace and love? So let our con-ver-sa-tion be; The ser-pent blend-ed with the dove, Wis-dom and meek sim-plic-i-ty.

lines: And is the gospel peace and love?
The serpent blended with the dove,
And tempt our thoughts or tongues to strife,
On Jesus let us fix our eyes,
Bright pattern of the Christian life!
How mild! how ready to forgive!
Be this the temper of our mind,
And his the rules by which we live.
The labors of his life were love;
If, then, we love our Saviour's name
Thus let us our relation prove.

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
